findings.title: Authorization bypass: 'and' changed to 'or' lets any viewer open any active document
findings.body: Triggering condition: any call where the document is active but the viewer is not the owner, e.g. can_open("user-1", "user-2", True). Base returned False (owner_id == viewer_id and active); target returns True because owner_id == viewer_id or active short-circuits to True whenever active is truthy. Consequence: an authorization bypass — every active document is openable by every viewer, directly violating the docstring contract "Only the owner of an active document may open it". Inactive documents are unaffected (both versions return False for active=False), so the regression is precisely the non-owner + active case. Suggested fix: restore the conjunction: return owner_id == viewer_id and active.

findings.title: size == 0 no longer rejected with ValueError; raises ZeroDivisionError instead
findings.body: Triggering condition: page_count(any_total, 0) — e.g. page_count(10, 0) or page_count(0, 0). Base raised ValueError("size must be positive") for size <= 0, matching the docstring "reject a nonpositive page size with ValueError". Target only rejects size < 0, so size == 0 falls through to '(total + size - 1) // size', and integer floor division by zero raises ZeroDivisionError regardless of the numerator. Consequence: the documented exception contract is broken; callers that validate inputs per the docstring or handle 'except ValueError' now receive an unhandled ZeroDivisionError (different type, different semantics). Negative sizes still raise ValueError, so only the size == 0 case regressed. Suggested fix: restore the guard 'if size <= 0:'.
